title: The Lamp at Gull Point
note: Synthetic fixture written for the router benchmark (scripts/router_benchmark.py). Four chapters of two scenes each, a codex with one entry hidden from AI, binder statuses and one synopsis.

chapters.title: Chapter One
chapters.synopsis: Mara arrives at Gull Point and meets the innkeeper and the keeper.

scenes.title: Arrival
paragraphs: The evening ferry pushed through grey water toward Gull Point, and the lighthouse stood dark against the cliffs. Nobody on deck spoke.
Mara Quill held her suitcase on her knees and counted the gulls. She had not seen the Point since she was a child, and she did not like the way the tower watched the harbour.
At the inn, Bram Hollis poured her a cup of tea and said the keeper would not see visitors. The innkeeper's hands shook when he mentioned the lamp.

scenes.title: The Keeper
paragraphs: Tom Vane opened the tower door only wide enough to look at her. He refused to say why the lamp had gone dark.
On a nail inside the door hung a brass key, green at the edges. Tom saw her looking and closed the door.
That night she wrote in her notebook that he was afraid of something, and that it was not the sea.

scenes.title: Night Watch
paragraphs: At midnight the lamp failed again. Mara climbed the hill in the rain and found the tower door unlocked.
From the gallery she could see the whole harbour, the ferry lights and the black rocks the lamp was meant to warn against.
Tom found her there and did not shout. He only said that the lens was older than both of them.

scenes.title: Letters
paragraphs: In the desk Mara found a bundle of letters tied with string. They were from her father, written the winter before he drowned.
One letter asked Tom to keep the key safe until his daughter came. Another was signed only with the name Edwin.
She put the letters back exactly as she had found them and told no one.

scenes.title: Storm
paragraphs: The storm came in on the third day. Waves broke over the harbour wall and the ferry stayed in port.
Mara asked Tom about the brass key, and he said he had lost it years ago. It was hanging on the nail behind him as he spoke.
She did not call him a liar. She asked him instead to teach her how to light the lamp by hand.

scenes.title: The Wreck
paragraphs: Near dawn a fishing boat struck the rocks below the tower. Bram rowed out with two men from the inn.
Mara held the lamp steady while Tom turned the lens, and the light reached the water in time.
They brought one survivor ashore, a young woman wrapped in a sail.

scenes.title: Ashore
paragraphs: The survivor said her name was Ada Lindqvist and that she had come to find the keeper.
Ada carried a letter in the same hand as the bundle in the desk. Mara read it twice before she understood it.
Tom sat down on the stairs and finally told her the truth about her father.

scenes.title: Morning
paragraphs: In the morning the storm had passed and the harbour was flat and bright.
Mara decided to stay through the winter. Bram said the inn would keep her room.
That evening she lit the lamp herself, and the brass key went back on its nail.
